result.summary: Implemented apps/bot/src/i18n/ (catalogs, resolveLang, parity Vitest test), apps/bot/src/domain/ (framework-free setUserLang, getUserWithChapterByTgId), apps/bot/src/handlers/ (start stub explicitly marked throwaway, lang command+callback). AC1 verified via npm test 13/13 plus a deliberate-break/revert cycle. AC5 verified: apps/web/messages unchanged, no packages/ dir created. AC2/3/4 verified via a real fixture DB (docker-compose scratch Postgres) but with the Telegram TRANSPORT mocked (a Context-shaped stub calling the real handler/domain/i18n code, since no real Telegram bot token was available) -- real SQL reads/writes and real handler logic exercised, Telegram wire protocol itself not exercised. Flagged explicitly for REVIEWER scrutiny since this diverges from what the design's SS3.3 assumed (a live bot instance).

issues.description: AC2/AC3/AC4 verification used a mocked grammY Context (no real Telegram token available in this environment) rather than a genuinely live bot instance as the design's verification method described. Real handler/domain/i18n code and real Postgres reads/writes were exercised; only the Telegram transport layer was stubbed. Flagged for REVIEWER/TEST-RUNNER/RELEASE-VALIDATOR to judge whether this satisfies AC2/AC4's literal 'live bot instance'/'sending /start' wording or whether a real bot token needs to be sourced.
